- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 3–5 days of forecast, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–2% downward correction for days 1–7 if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint.
